items.stem: Which term matches this description: "An index produced by UNDP and OPHI measuring deprivation in health, education and living standards; MPI = H × A"?
items.answer: Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI)
items.markingKey: A. This is the definition of Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI).

items.stem: A student claims: "A Gini coefficient of 0.5 means half the population is poor." Identify the error in this claim and correct it.
items.answer: It measures the distribution of income, not the proportion of people in poverty.
items.markingKey: It measures the distribution of income, not the proportion of people in poverty. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: With the help of a specific example, explain why the GII is useful for understanding development.
items.answer: It reveals gender gaps hidden in national averages - maternal mortality, adolescent births, parliamentary seats, secondary education and labour force participation - which constrain development. (A specific, correct example that illustrates this is required for full marks.)
items.markingKey: Award marks for: It reveals gender gaps hidden in national averages - maternal mortality, adolescent births, parliamentary seats, secondary education and labour force participation - which constrain development. (A specific, correct example that illustrates this is required for full marks.) (3 marks: one for each linked point in the chain of reasoning; no marks for assertion without explanation.)

items.stem: Using named countries, explain why using several indicators gives a better picture of development than using one.
items.answer: e.g. Qatar has very high GNI per capita but a lower HDI rank and high gender inequality; Cuba has modest income but high life expectancy and education; South Africa's HDI is medium-high but its Gini is about 0.63 and multidimensional poverty persists.
items.markingKey: e.g. Qatar has very high GNI per capita but a lower HDI rank and high gender inequality; Cuba has modest income but high life expectancy and education; South Africa's HDI is medium-high but its Gini is about 0.63 and multidimensional poverty persists.

items.stem: Approximate data for Ethiopia: life expectancy 65.0 years; expected years of schooling 9.4; mean years of schooling 3.2; GNI per capita US$2,400 (PPP). Using the UNDP method - life expectancy index = (LE − 20)/65; education index = (MYS/15 + EYS/18)/2, with EYS capped at 18; income index = (ln GNI − ln 100)/(ln 75,000 − ln 100); HDI = geometric mean of the three indices - calculate the HDI and its category.
items.markingKey: A1 LEI 0.692; A1 EI 0.368; A1 II 0.480; M1 geometric mean; A1 HDI 0.496, low.

items.stem: Briefly analyse two contrasting points of view on the statement: "Income inequality is the greatest barrier to development."
items.answer: Inequality is a major barrier, but poverty levels, governance and conflict are also crucial.
items.markingKey: For: high Gini limits poverty reduction (South Africa, Brazil). Against: absolute poverty, conflict and governance also matter. [4]: 1 mark for a valid argument for, 1 for its development; 1 mark for a valid argument against, 1 for its development; generic points without geographical context are capped at 2.

items.stem: "The HDI is the most useful measure of human development." Discuss this statement, with reference to examples you have studied.
items.answer: HDI is a useful starting point, but must be used with IHDI, GII, MPI and Gini.
items.markingKey: Indicative content - for: combines three dimensions; widely available data allow comparisons. Against / limitations: ignores inequality, gender, environment and freedom; national averages hide internal differences. A supported conclusion might be: HDI is a useful starting point, but must be used with IHDI, GII, MPI and Gini. items.stem: State what is meant by the term "Human Development Index (HDI)".
items.answer: A UNDP composite index (0-1) combining life expectancy, education (expected and mean years of schooling) and GNI per capita (PPP)
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the core idea: a UNDP composite index (0-1) combining life expectancy, education (expected and mean years of schooling) and GNI per capita (PPP). Award full marks only if the defining feature is clear; a vague example alone scores 0.

items.stem: Briefly explain why a high GNI per capita does not always mean low inequality.
items.answer: GNI per capita is an average that ignores distribution; income may be concentrated among a wealthy elite, as shown by high Gini coefficients in countries such as South Africa and Brazil.
items.markingKey: Award marks for: GNI per capita is an average that ignores distribution; income may be concentrated among a wealthy elite, as shown by high Gini coefficients in countries such as South Africa and Brazil. (2 marks: one for each linked point in the chain of reasoning; no marks for assertion without explanation.)

items.stem: Explain the difference between the Gini coefficient and GNI per capita.
items.answer: GNI per capita measures average income; the Gini coefficient measures how evenly income is distributed among the population.
items.markingKey: GNI per capita measures average income; the Gini coefficient measures how evenly income is distributed among the population. One mark for a correct account of each side; further marks for making the difference explicit (not two separate definitions).

items.stem: With reference to Niger, explain how it illustrates low human development.
items.answer: It has one of the lowest HDI scores (about 0.39) and over 60% of people are multidimensionally poor. Low life expectancy, schooling and income combine with high fertility and climate stress.
items.markingKey: Context (It has one of the lowest HDI scores (about 0.39) and over 60% of people are multidimensionally poor.) – 1 mark for accurate, specific detail. Link: Low life expectancy, schooling and income combine with high fertility and climate stress. – remaining marks for explicitly connecting the example to low human development.

items.stem: Income shares by quintile (poorest to richest 20%) in an illustrative data set modelled on Sweden: 3%, 14%, 15%, 18%, 50%. Calculate the cumulative shares and estimate the Gini coefficient using G = 1 − Σ (Xk − Xk−1)(Yk + Yk−1), where X steps by 0.2.
items.markingKey: M1 cumulative shares; M1 trapezium sum; A1 G ≈ 0.392.

items.stem: Which country's growth since 1978 lifted about 800 million people out of extreme poverty?
items.answer: China
items.markingKey: China. World Bank estimate (2022).

items.stem: Explain how trade can promote development.
items.answer: Exports bring foreign exchange, jobs and investment; access to larger markets allows economies of scale; technology transfer; e.g. the export-led growth of South Korea and Vietnam.
items.markingKey: Award marks for: Exports bring foreign exchange, jobs and investment; access to larger markets allows economies of scale; technology transfer; e.g. the export-led growth of South Korea and Vietnam. items.stem: "Trade always benefits low-income countries." Explain the flaw in this statement.
items.answer: Gains depend on what is traded; dependence on raw commodities and unfair rules can limit benefits.
items.markingKey: Gains depend on what is traded; dependence on raw commodities and unfair rules can limit benefits. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: In a recent year the UK provided about US$19.0 billion of official development assistance; its GNI was about US$3,330 billion. Calculate ODA as a percentage of GNI and compare it with the UN target of 0.7%.
items.answer: 0.57% of GNI - below the 0.7% target
items.markingKey: M1 ODA ÷ GNI × 100; A1 0.57%; R1 comparison.

items.markingKey: M1 (new − old) ÷ old × 100 = (482.5 − 307.6) ÷ 307.6 × 100; A1 +56.9% (sign or "increase/decrease" required).

items.stem: To what extent do you agree that empowering women is the most effective strategy for development?
items.answer: Women's empowerment is among the most effective strategies, but it works best alongside economic and political reforms.
items.markingKey: Indicative content - for: multiplier effects on health, education and income; demographic dividend. items.answer: conditional cash transfer
items.markingKey: B. This is the definition of conditional cash transfer.

items.stem: Explain the difference between bottom-up development and top-down development.
items.answer: Top-down development is planned by governments or agencies, often large-scale (dams, highways); bottom-up development is led by local communities, small-scale and uses local knowledge (wells, co-operatives).
items.markingKey: Top-down development is planned by governments or agencies, often large-scale (dams, highways); bottom-up development is led by local communities, small-scale and uses local knowledge (wells, co-operatives). One mark for a correct account of each side; further marks for making the difference explicit (not two separate definitions).

items.stem: Briefly explain why aid does not always lead to development.
items.answer: Aid may be tied, poorly targeted, captured by elites, create dependency or fund prestige projects; donor priorities may not match local needs.
items.markingKey: Award marks for: Aid may be tied, poorly targeted, captured by elites, create dependency or fund prestige projects; donor priorities may not match local needs. (2 marks: one for each linked point in the chain of reasoning; no marks for assertion without explanation.)

items.stem: Outline one way in which Brazil's Bolsa Família shows social policy for development.
items.answer: Conditional cash transfers to about 14 million families helped cut extreme poverty and raise school attendance. Targeted transfers reduced poverty and inequality.
items.markingKey: Context (Conditional cash transfers to about 14 million families helped cut extreme poverty and raise school attendance.) – 1 mark for accurate, specific detail. Link: Targeted transfers reduced poverty and inequality. – remaining marks for explicitly connecting the example to social policy for development.

items.stem: Suggest how conditional cash transfers can reduce poverty over the long term.
items.answer: Conditions on school attendance and health check-ups increase human capital so the next generation earns more, breaking the cycle of poverty.
items.markingKey: Conditions on school attendance and health check-ups increase human capital so the next generation earns more, breaking the cycle of poverty.

items.stem: "Trade is more effective than aid in promoting development." To what extent do you agree with this statement? In your answer, consider the perspectives of different places and scales.
items.answer: Trade drives long-term growth, but aid remains important for public goods and the poorest countries.
items.markingKey: Paper 3 (b) indicative content - for: East Asian export-led growth; aid dependency risks. Against: aid funds health and education that markets underprovide; trade rules can disadvantage poor countries. Judgement: Trade drives long-term growth, but aid remains important for public goods and the poorest countries. items.stem: Which of the following best describes "human rights"?
options: 17 UN goals with 169 targets adopted in 2015 to achieve by 2030, including ending poverty, hunger and inequality
A UNDP composite index (0-1) combining life expectancy, education (expected and mean years of schooling) and GNI per capita (PPP)
Living on less than US$2.15 a day (2017 PPP), the World Bank international poverty line
The basic rights and freedoms belonging to every person, set out in the 1948 Universal Declaration of Human Rights
items.answer: The basic rights and freedoms belonging to every person, set out in the 1948 Universal Declaration of Human Rights
items.markingKey: D. "human rights" is the basic rights and freedoms belonging to every person, set out in the 1948 Universal Declaration of Human Rights.

items.stem: Explain the difference between the SDGs and the MDGs.
items.answer: The MDGs (2000-2015) had 8 goals focused mainly on poverty, health and education in developing countries; the SDGs (2015-2030) have 17 universal goals including sustainability, inequality and governance.
items.markingKey: The MDGs (2000-2015) had 8 goals focused mainly on poverty, health and education in developing countries; the SDGs (2015-2030) have 17 universal goals including sustainability, inequality and governance. One mark for a correct account of each side; further marks for making the difference explicit (not two separate definitions).

items.stem: With the help of a specific example, explain why indigenous peoples often have lower development indicators.
items.answer: Historic land dispossession, discrimination, remoteness from services, language barriers and lack of political representation, e.g. Aboriginal Australians' lower life expectancy. (A specific, correct example that illustrates this is required for full marks.)
items.markingKey: Award marks for: Historic land dispossession, discrimination, remoteness from services, language barriers and lack of political representation, e.g. Aboriginal Australians' lower life expectancy. items.stem: Briefly explain why human rights are linked to development.
items.answer: Rights to education, health, work and political participation build capabilities (Sen's "development as freedom"); discrimination and denial of rights limit people's ability to escape poverty.

items.answer: Trade involves earning income by selling goods and services in markets; aid is a transfer of resources from donors that does not need to be earned.

items.markingKey: Growth can coexist with abuses of labour, gender or political rights; rights need laws and institutions. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.answer: Indicative content: SDGs and their targets; rights to education, health, gender equality; examples (child marriage, indigenous peoples, Ethiopia, China); barriers to progress.

Paper 1 extended-response markbands [10]: 9-10 responds to all demands of the question; accurate, detailed knowledge and understanding; well-developed, relevant examples and case studies with specific (named, located, quantified) detail; balanced, well-structured evaluation leading to a substantiated conclusion. 7-8 responds to most demands; mostly accurate knowledge; examples relevant but not always fully developed; evaluation present but uneven. 5-6 some demands addressed; knowledge partly accurate; examples general or loosely linked; evaluation mostly implicit. 3-4 limited, largely descriptive; little use of examples. 1-2 little relevant knowledge or understanding. 0 does not reach the standard of the descriptors.

items.stem: "Income inequality is the greatest barrier to development." To what extent do you agree with this statement? In your answer, consider the perspectives of people in high- and low-income countries.
items.answer: Inequality is a major barrier, but poverty levels, governance and conflict are also crucial.
items.markingKey: Paper 3 (b) indicative content - for: high Gini limits poverty reduction (South Africa, Brazil); unequal access to health and education. Against: absolute poverty, conflict and governance also matter; some unequal countries still develop rapidly (China). Judgement: Inequality is a major barrier, but poverty levels, governance and conflict are also crucial. Markbands [16]: 14-16 well-structured, balanced argument that synthesises HL concepts (power, places, processes, possibilities) across scales; perspectives evaluated explicitly; detailed, located evidence; substantiated conclusion. 11-13 balanced with developed evidence but synthesis uneven. 8-10 some evaluation, evidence partly developed. 5-7 mainly descriptive. 1-4 little relevant knowledge.

items.stem: Explain the arguments that geographers use to support the view that trade is more effective than aid in promoting development.
items.answer: East Asian export-led growth; aid dependency risks
items.markingKey: Paper 3 (a) indicative content: East Asian export-led growth; aid dependency risks; aid funds health and education that markets underprovide; trade rules can disadvantage poor countries. Markbands [12]: 10-12 detailed, accurate explanation with well-developed, located examples and clear links between factors; 7-9 accurate explanation, examples partly developed; 4-6 some relevant knowledge, mostly descriptive; 1-3 little relevant knowledge.

items.stem: Which dimension is NOT part of the HDI?
options: Mean and expected years of schooling
items.answer: Gender equality
items.markingKey: B. Gender is measured separately by the GII and GDI.

items.stem: Which of the following best describes "trade liberalisation"?
options: The 1948 UN document setting out 30 articles of fundamental human rights
The HDI discounted for inequality in each dimension within a country
The reduction of barriers to trade such as tariffs and quotas to integrate an economy into global markets
A measure of income inequality from 0 (perfect equality) to 1 (one person has all income), derived from the Lorenz curve
items.answer: The reduction of barriers to trade such as tariffs and quotas to integrate an economy into global markets
items.markingKey: C. "trade liberalisation" is the reduction of barriers to trade such as tariffs and quotas to integrate an economy into global markets.

items.stem: Which term matches this description: "The 1948 UN document setting out 30 articles of fundamental human rights"?
items.answer: Universal Declaration of Human Rights
items.markingKey: A. This is the definition of Universal Declaration of Human Rights.

items.stem: Distinguish between the Gini coefficient and GNI per capita.
items.answer: GNI per capita measures average income; the Gini coefficient measures how evenly income is distributed among the population.
items.markingKey: GNI per capita measures average income; the Gini coefficient measures how evenly income is distributed among the population. One mark for a correct account of each side; further marks for making the difference explicit (not two separate definitions).

items.stem: Briefly explain why the empowerment of women is important for development.
items.answer: Educated women have fewer, healthier children, invest more in families, increase household incomes and labour force participation, and influence decision-making - multiplier effects across health, education and the economy.
items.markingKey: Award marks for: Educated women have fewer, healthier children, invest more in families, increase household incomes and labour force participation, and influence decision-making - multiplier effects across health, education and the economy. (2 marks: one for each linked point in the chain of reasoning; no marks for assertion without explanation.)

items.stem: Distinguish between the SDGs and the MDGs.
items.answer: The MDGs (2000-2015) had 8 goals focused mainly on poverty, health and education in developing countries; the SDGs (2015-2030) have 17 universal goals including sustainability, inequality and governance.
items.markingKey: The MDGs (2000-2015) had 8 goals focused mainly on poverty, health and education in developing countries; the SDGs (2015-2030) have 17 universal goals including sustainability, inequality and governance. One mark for a correct account of each side; further marks for making the difference explicit (not two separate definitions).

items.stem: "A Gini coefficient of 0.5 means half the population is poor." Explain the flaw in this statement.
items.answer: It measures the distribution of income, not the proportion of people in poverty.
items.markingKey: It measures the distribution of income, not the proportion of people in poverty. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: Explain the difference between aid and trade.
items.answer: Trade involves earning income by selling goods and services in markets; aid is a transfer of resources from donors that does not need to be earned.
items.markingKey: Trade involves earning income by selling goods and services in markets; aid is a transfer of resources from donors that does not need to be earned. One mark for a correct account of each side; further marks for making the difference explicit (not two separate definitions).

items.stem: Briefly explain why progress towards the SDGs has slowed since 2020.
items.answer: COVID-19 reversed poverty and education gains, conflict (Ukraine, Sudan, Gaza) and climate disasters displaced millions, food and energy prices rose, and debt limited government spending.
items.markingKey: Award marks for: COVID-19 reversed poverty and education gains, conflict (Ukraine, Sudan, Gaza) and climate disasters displaced millions, food and energy prices rose, and debt limited government spending. (2 marks: one for each linked point in the chain of reasoning; no marks for assertion without explanation.)

items.stem: Suggest why the HDI of oil-rich Gulf states ranks lower than their GNI per capita.
items.answer: Education indicators, especially mean years of schooling among older adults, are lower than in other countries with similar incomes.
items.markingKey: Education indicators, especially mean years of schooling among older adults, are lower than in other countries with similar incomes.

items.stem: With reference to Vietnam's Doi Moi reforms, explain how it illustrates trade and investment-led development.
items.answer: From 1986 market reforms and FDI turned it into a major exporter, and extreme poverty fell from about 50% to under 5%. Opening to trade and FDI drove rapid poverty reduction.
items.markingKey: Context (From 1986 market reforms and FDI turned it into a major exporter, and extreme poverty fell from about 50% to under 5%.) – 1 mark for accurate, specific detail. Link: Opening to trade and FDI drove rapid poverty reduction. – remaining marks for explicitly connecting the example to trade and investment-led development.

items.stem: Between 1990 and 2010 the number of births registered in a province of Italy changed from 7,488 to 12,073 births. Calculate the percentage change over the period.
items.markingKey: M1 (new − old) ÷ old × 100 = (12,073 − 7,488) ÷ 7,488 × 100; A1 +61.2% (sign or "increase/decrease" required).

items.stem: Approximate data for Japan: life expectancy 84.8 years; expected years of schooling 15.2; mean years of schooling 13.4; GNI per capita US$44,000 (PPP). Using the UNDP method - life expectancy index = (LE − 20)/65; education index = (MYS/15 + EYS/18)/2, with EYS capped at 18; income index = (ln GNI − ln 100)/(ln 75,000 − ln 100); HDI = geometric mean of the three indices - calculate the HDI and its category.
items.markingKey: A1 LEI 0.997; A1 EI 0.869; A1 II 0.919; M1 geometric mean; A1 HDI 0.927, very high.

items.stem: A data table shows the internet users in a South-East Asian archipelago state: 1995 - 77.1 million; 2015 - 163.2 million. Calculate the percentage change over the period.
items.markingKey: M1 (new − old) ÷ old × 100 = (163.2 − 77.1) ÷ 77.1 × 100; A1 +111.7% (sign or "increase/decrease" required).

items.stem: Suggest why measuring progress towards the SDGs is difficult.
items.answer: Many indicators lack data in poorer countries; 169 targets are complex; national averages hide inequalities; definitions vary.
items.markingKey: Many indicators lack data in poorer countries; 169 targets are complex; national averages hide inequalities; definitions vary.

items.stem: In a division of Bangladesh, 22% of people are multidimensionally poor (headcount, H) and the poor are deprived in an average of 61% of the weighted indicators (intensity, A). Calculate the Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI = H × A). Ten years later H has fallen to 5% with no change in intensity: calculate the new MPI and the percentage reduction.
Give one strength and one weakness of the claim that trade is more effective than aid in promoting development.
items.answer: Trade drives long-term growth, but aid remains important for public goods and the poorest countries.
items.markingKey: For: East Asian export-led growth. Against: aid funds health and education that markets underprovide. [4]: 1 mark for a valid argument for, 1 for its development; 1 mark for a valid argument against, 1 for its development; generic points without geographical context are capped at 2.

items.stem:
Study the infographic / visual stimulus described below.

Table: people in extreme poverty (millions, World Bank, US$2.15/day) - 1990: 2,000; 2010: 1,140; 2019: 670; 2022: 712.

(a) Calculate the percentage change from 1990 to 2019. [4]
(b) Using the resource and your own knowledge, suggest reasons for the increase after 2019. [6]
items.answer: (a) (670 − 2,000)/2,000 × 100 = -66.5% (b) COVID-19 job losses, rising food and energy prices after the war in Ukraine, conflict and debt crises.
items.markingKey: (a) (670 − 2,000)/2,000 × 100 = -66.5% (b) COVID-19 job losses, rising food and energy prices after the war in Ukraine, conflict and debt crises. Credit relevant own knowledge and named examples in (b). Infographic markscheme [10]: part (a) [4] - award 1 mark per valid point taken from the resource (data must be quoted with units for full marks); part (b) [6] - up to 2 marks for each developed explanation linking the resource to own knowledge; reward named examples; maximum 3 marks if the resource is not used.

items.answer: high Gini limits poverty reduction (South Africa, Brazil); unequal access to health and education
